10.1002_adma.75576: (CIGS) tandem solar cells have emerged as a highly promising thin-film photovoltaic architecture, combining the exceptional efficiency potential of perovskites with the industrial maturity of CIGS technology. Despite rapid advances in perovskite top cells, overall tandem performance remains fundamentally constrained by the CIGS bottom cell, which critically governs bandgap matching, voltage losses, and interfacial recombination. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent progress in CIGS absorber and interface engineering for tandem applications. We highlight key strategies including Ga-gradient bandgap engineering, alkali post-deposition treatment, Ag alloying for low-temperature growth and bifacial operation, as well as buffer-layer and intermediate recombination layer optimization. We further discuss how surface morphology and defect chemistry collectively dictate carrier recombination dynamics and interfacial stability in monolithic device architectures. Finally, we outline a roadmap toward the commercialization of perovskite/CIGS tandem photovoltaics. By linking materials-level engineering with device-level constraints, this review establishes a unified framework to guide the development of high-efficiency, scalable, and industrially viable tandem solar technologies.
10.1002_advs.78666: Wearable electronics and soft bioelectronics require stretchable devices with steady performance under deformation. However, the balance between electrical performance and stretchability remains a critical obstacle, and most approaches sacrifice charge transport mobility to achieve stretchability. Herein, we present a material design concept that utilizes a wet‐spinning strategy to fabricate highly stretchable semiconducting polymer fibers, enabling high‐performance organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) with stable or even enhanced charge transport mobility under large strains. The polymer chains are ordered within the fibers under the shear effects of the spinning fluid and can reorient during stretching to dissipate strain energy, further forming a more compact and ordered molecular arrangement. As a result, the fabricated semiconductor fiber can be stretched to over 250% strain and exhibit an ultrahigh normalized transconductance of 276.4 S cm −1 , far exceeding thin‐film polymer semiconductors. More importantly, the fiber OECTs possess unique strain‐enhanced electrical performance, with substantially improved charge carrier mobility after strain‐induced ordered arrangement of molecular chains. The skin‐like fully stretchable OECTs have been successfully applied for recording electrocardiogram signals. This work provides more possibilities for the further development of stretchable semiconducting polymer materials with high electrical performance.
10.1002_aenm.202570020: Tandem Solar Cells In article number 2303021, Zhiqin Ying, Xi Yang, Jichun Ye, and co-workers developed an oblique-angle damage-free evaporation technique to deposit a conformal, ultra-thin SiOX layer without causing damage to the underlying perovskite. This SiOX interlayer serves as both a chemical and field-effect passivation layer while also acting as a dense inner encapsulation layer, significantly enhancing the photovoltaic efficiency and stability of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.
10.1002_aenm.71330: The large‐scale deployment of redox flow batteries (RFBs) remains constrained by sluggish catalytic kinetics within carbon felt electrodes, causing severe polarization losses. Addressing this necessitates system‐specific electrode activation strategies tailored to the distinct mechanisms of various redox couples. This review systematically analyzes catalyst modification advancements across four key RFB configurations: vanadium, zinc‐based, iron‐based, and organic systems. We establish definitive mechanistic pathways by correlating performance enhancements with specific electrochemical activation dynamics. Specifically, vanadium RFBs leverage atomic‐scale defect engineering and Bi‐centric catalysis to accelerate reaction kinetics. Zinc‐based systems employ zincophilic nanostructures (e.g., CuO) to ensure uniform nucleation and suppress dendrite growth. Iron‐based architectures integrate high hydrogen evolution overpotential materials, such as Pb and Bi, to mitigate parasitic reactions. Finally, organic RFBs focus on advanced surface functionalization to maximize active site density and stability. By synthesizing these strategies, this work provides comprehensive guidelines for optimizing electrode functionality across distinct RFB architectures.
